title: Block sliding to a stop on a deformable plate, friction decaying with the slip rate (explicit contact)
source: A rigid block launched at v₀ with friction μ(v) = μk + (μs − μk) e^(−d v) decelerates at g μ(v); it travels ∫₀^v₀ v dv / (g μ(v)) (Simpson's rule, 200 000 intervals) and stops after [v₀ + ln((μk + (μs − μk) e^(−d v₀))/μs)/d]/(g μk) = 1.2001; Meriam & Kraige, Engineering Mechanics: Dynamics, §3/5; the exponential decay law as in Oden & Martins, CMAME 52:527–634, 1985

quantities.quantity: distance travelled (top centre node) against ∫ v dv / (g μ(v)) = 2.01524
quantities.reason: the block bounces on the penalty springs and the plate under it shears elastically, so the normal force and the slip rate it feels vary by a little around their rigid-body values

quantities.quantity: velocity of the top centre node after the stop
quantities.reason: the block sticks; what is left is its elastic vibration, under 1% of v₀
